Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version

use clap::{value_parser, Arg, ArgAction, Command, ValueHint};

use crate::langs::Language;

pub const FIELDS: &[&str] = &[
    "project",
    "description",
    "head",
    "pending",
    "version",
    "created",
    "languages",
    "dependencies",
    "authors",
    "last-change",
    "contributors",
    "url",
    "commits",
    "churn",
    "lines-of-code",
    "size",
    "license",
];

pub fn build_command() -> Command {
    let lang_values: Vec<&'static str> = Language::all().iter().map(|l| l.cli_name()).collect();
    Command::new("onefetch")
        .version("2.25.0")
        .about("Command-line Git information tool")
        .arg(
            Arg::new("input")
                .value_name("INPUT")
                .help("Run as if onefetch was started in <input> instead of the current working directory")
                .value_hint(ValueHint::DirPath)
                .value_parser(value_parser!(std::path::PathBuf)),
        )
        .next_help_heading("INFO")
        .arg(
            Arg::new("disabled_fields")
                .short('d')
                .long("disabled-fields")
                .value_name("FIELD")
                .help("Allows you to disable FIELD(s) from appearing in the output")
                .num_args(1..)
                .action(ArgAction::Append)
                .value_parser(FIELDS.to_vec()),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("no_title")
                .long("no-title")
                .help("Hides the title")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("number_of_authors")
                .long("number-of-authors")
                .value_name("NUM")
                .help("Maximum NUM of authors to be shown")
                .default_value("3")
                .value_parser(value_parser!(usize)),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("number_of_languages")
                .long("number-of-languages")
                .value_name("NUM")
                .help("Maximum NUM of languages to be shown")
                .default_value("6")
                .value_parser(value_parser!(usize)),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("number_of_file_churns")
                .long("number-of-file-churns")
                .value_name("NUM")
                .help("Maximum NUM of file churns to be shown")
                .default_value("3")
                .value_parser(value_parser!(usize)),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("churn_pool_size")
                .long("churn-pool-size")
                .value_name("NUM")
                .help("Minimum NUM of commits from HEAD used to compute the churn summary")
                .long_help("Minimum NUM of commits from HEAD used to compute the churn summary\n\nBy default, the actual value is non-deterministic due to time-based computation and will be displayed under the info title \"Churn (NUM)\"")
                .value_parser(value_parser!(usize)),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("exclude")
                .short('e')
                .long("exclude")
                .value_name("EXCLUDE")
                .help("Ignore all files & directories matching EXCLUDE")
                .num_args(1..)
                .action(ArgAction::Append),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("no_bots")
                .long("no-bots")
                .value_name("REGEX")
                .help("Exclude [bot] commits. Use <REGEX> to override the default pattern")
                .num_args(0..=1)
                .require_equals(true)
                .default_missing_value("(?:-|\\s)[Bb]ot$|\\[[Bb]ot\\]"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("no_merges")
                .long("no-merges")
                .help("Ignores merge commits")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("email")

import json

 "data": ['ABNF', 'Graphql', 'Json', 'Sql', 'Svg', 'Toml', 'Xaml', 'Xml', 'Yaml'],
}
def kind(name):
    for k, v in TYPES.items():
        if name in v: return {"markup": "Markup", "prose": "Prose", "data": "Data"}[k]
    return "Programming"
JUPYTER = {"icon": "\ue80f", "rgb": [218, 91, 11]}
def parse_code(c):
    # returns ("rgb",(r,g,b)) or ("ansi", code)
    parts = c.split(";")
    if parts[0] == "38" and parts[1] == "2":
        return ("rgb", tuple(int(x) for x in parts[2:5]))
    return ("ansi", int(parts[0]))
out = []
out.append("// Generated language data. Do not edit by hand.\n")
out.append("use super::{LangDef, LanguageType};\n")
out.append("pub const LANGS: &[LangDef] = &[\n")
for row in table:
    name = row["json"]
    basic = [parse_code(c) for c in row["probe_basic"]]
    truec = [parse_code(c) for c in row["probe_true"]]
    # defined basic colors: strip trailing (ansi,39) entries
    b = [c for c in basic]
    while b and b[-1] == ("ansi", 39): b.pop()
    # true colors: leading rgb entries
    t = []
    for c in truec:
        if c[0] == "rgb": t.append(c[1])
        else: break
    # sanity: beyond t, true probe should equal basic probe
    for i in range(len(t), len(truec)):
        assert truec[i] == basic[i], (name, truec, basic)
    nb = max(len(b), 1)
    basic_codes = [c[1] if c[0] == "ansi" else None for c in basic[:nb]]
    assert all(x is not None for x in basic_codes), (name, basic)
    icon = row["icon"]; chip = row["chip_rgb"]
    if name == "Jupyter": icon, chip = JUPYTER["icon"], JUPYTER["rgb"]
    if name == "Text": icon, chip = None, None
    art = "\n".join(row["art"]["template"])
    def rs_str(s):
        return '"' + s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n").replace("{", "{{").replace("}", "}}") + '"'
    # careful: we don't use format! so no need to escape braces
    def rs_str2(s):
        return '"' + s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n") + '"'
    def rs_char_str(s):
        if s is None: return "None"
        return "Some(" + rs_str2(s) + ")"
    tc = "&[" + ", ".join("(%d, %d, %d)" % c for c in t) + "]"
    chip_s = "None" if chip is None else "Some((%d, %d, %d))" % tuple(chip)
    out.append("    LangDef {\n")
    out.append("        name: %s,\n" % rs_str2(name))
    out.append("        display: %s,\n" % rs_str2(row["display"]))
    out.append("        cli: %s,\n" % rs_str2(row["cli"]))
    out.append("        kind: LanguageType::%s,\n" % kind(name))
    out.append("        ascii: %s,\n" % rs_str2(art))
    out.append("        basic: &[%s],\n" % ", ".join(str(c) for c in basic_codes))
    out.append("        truecolor: %s,\n" % tc)
    out.append("        chip: %s,\n" % chip_s)
    out.append("        icon: %s,\n" % rs_char_str(icon))
    out.append("    },\n")
out.append("];\n")
open("/workspace/src/langs/data.rs", "w").write("".join(out))
print("ok", len(table))

    art = "\n".join(row["art"]["template"])

    tc = "&[" + ", ".join("(%d, %d, %d)" % c for c in t) + "]"
    chip_s = "None" if chip is None else "Some((%d, %d, %d))" % tuple(chip)
    out.append("    LangDef {\n")

    out.append("        icon: %s,\n" % rs_char_str(icon))
    out.append("    },\n")

//! Per-language syntax definitions and file type detection.

use crate::langs::Language;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::Path;
use std::sync::OnceLock;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum Context {
    None,
    Markdown,
    Html,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Syntax {
    pub line_comments: &'static [&'static str],
    pub multi_line_comments: &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)],
    pub nested: bool,
    pub nested_comments: &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)],
    pub quotes: &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)],
    pub verbatim_quotes: &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)],
    pub doc_quotes: &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)],
    pub literate: bool,
    pub is_fortran: bool,
    pub fortran_legacy: bool,
    pub context: Context,
}

impl Syntax {
    pub fn has_important_syntax(&self, line: &[u8]) -> bool {
        let tokens = self
            .quotes
            .iter()
            .chain(self.verbatim_quotes.iter())
            .chain(self.doc_quotes.iter())
            .chain(self.multi_line_comments.iter())
            .chain(self.nested_comments.iter())
            .map(|(s, _)| *s);
        for t in tokens {
            if contains(line, t.as_bytes()) {
                return true;
            }
        }
        match self.context {
            Context::Markdown => contains(line, b"```"),
            Context::Html => contains(line, b"<script") || contains(line, b"<style"),
            Context::None => false,
        }
    }
}

fn contains(hay: &[u8], needle: &[u8]) -> bool {
    !needle.is_empty() && hay.len() >= needle.len() && hay.windows(needle.len()).any(|w| w == needle)
}

    ($lc:expr, $ml:expr, $nested:expr, $nc:expr, $q:expr, $vq:expr, $dq:expr, $lit:expr, $fortran:expr, $legacy:expr, $ctx:expr) => {

struct Tables {
    by_lang: HashMap<Language, &'static Def>,
    by_ext: HashMap<&'static str, Language>,
    by_name: HashMap<&'static str, Language>,
}

fn tables() -> &'static Tables {
    static T: OnceLock<Tables> = OnceLock::new();
    T.get_or_init(|| {
        let mut by_lang = HashMap::new();
        let mut by_ext = HashMap::new();
        let mut by_name = HashMap::new();
        for d in DEFS.iter() {
            if let Some(l) = Language::from_name(d.name) {
                by_lang.insert(l, d);
                for e in d.extensions {
                    by_ext.insert(*e, l);
                }
                for f in d.filenames {
                    by_name.insert(*f, l);
                }
            }
        }
        Tables {
            by_lang,
            by_ext,
            by_name,
        }
    })
}

pub fn syntax_for(lang: Language) -> &'static Syntax {
    tables()
        .by_lang
        .get(&lang)
        .map(|d| &d.syntax)
        .unwrap_or(&UNKNOWN_SYNTAX)
}

pub fn from_extension(ext: &str) -> Option<Language> {
    tables().by_ext.get(ext.to_lowercase().as_str()).copied()
}

pub fn language_from_path(path: &Path) -> Option<Language> {
    let fname = path.file_name()?.to_string_lossy().to_lowercase();
    if let Some(l) = tables().by_name.get(fname.as_str()) {
        return Some(*l);
    }
    match path.extension() {
        Some(ext) => from_extension(&ext.to_string_lossy()),
        None => from_shebang(path),
    }
}

fn from_shebang(path: &Path) -> Option<Language> {
    use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader};
    let f = std::fs::File::open(path).ok()?;
    let mut reader = BufReader::new(f);
    let mut buf = Vec::new();
    reader.read_until(b'\n', &mut buf).ok()?;
    let line = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf).to_string();
    let mut words = line.split_whitespace();
    let first = words.next()?;
    if first == "#!/usr/bin/env" {
        let word = words.next()?;
        for d in DEFS.iter() {
            for e in d.env {
                if word.starts_with(e) {
                    return Language::from_name(d.name);
                }
            }
        }
        None
    } else {
        for d in DEFS.iter() {
            if d.shebangs.contains(&first) {
                return Language::from_name(d.name);
            }
        }
        None
    }
}

//! Per-language syntax definitions and file type detection.

use crate::langs::Language;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::Path;
use std::sync::OnceLock;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum Context {
    None,
    Markdown,
    Html,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Syntax {
    pub line_comments: &'static [&'static str],
    pub multi_line_comments: &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)],
    pub nested: bool,
    pub nested_comments: &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)],
    pub quotes: &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)],
    pub verbatim_quotes: &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)],
    pub doc_quotes: &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)],
    pub literate: bool,
    pub is_fortran: bool,
    pub fortran_legacy: bool,
    pub context: Context,
}

impl Syntax {
    pub fn has_important_syntax(&self, line: &[u8]) -> bool {
        let tokens = self
            .quotes
            .iter()
            .chain(self.verbatim_quotes.iter())
            .chain(self.doc_quotes.iter())
            .chain(self.multi_line_comments.iter())
            .chain(self.nested_comments.iter())
            .map(|(s, _)| *s);
        for t in tokens {
            if contains(line, t.as_bytes()) {
                return true;
            }
        }
        match self.context {
            Context::Markdown => contains(line, b"```"),
            Context::Html => contains(line, b"<script") || contains(line, b"<style"),
            Context::None => false,
        }
    }
}

fn contains(hay: &[u8], needle: &[u8]) -> bool {
    !needle.is_empty() && hay.len() >= needle.len() && hay.windows(needle.len()).any(|w| w == needle)
}

const DQ: &[(&str, &str)] = &[("\"", "\"")];
const DQ_SQ: &[(&str, &str)] = &[("\"", "\""), ("'", "'")];

const HTML_ML: &[(&str, &str)] = &[("<!--", "-->")];
const SLASH: &[&str] = &["//"];
const HASH: &[&str] = &["#"];
const DASH: &[&str] = &["--"];
const SEMI: &[&str] = &[";"];
const PCT: &[&str] = &["%"];
const EMPTY: &[&str] = &[];

macro_rules! syn {
    ($lc:expr, $ml:expr, $nested:expr, $nc:expr, $q:expr, $vq:expr, $dq:expr, $lit:expr, $fortran:expr, $legacy:expr, $ctx:expr) => {

            nested_comments: $nc,

            literate: $lit,
            is_fortran: $fortran,
            fortran_legacy: $legacy,
            context: $ctx,

macro_rules! simple {

    ($lc:expr, $ml:expr, $q:expr, nested) => {

struct Tables {
    by_lang: HashMap<Language, &'static Def>,
    by_ext: HashMap<&'static str, Language>,
    by_name: HashMap<&'static str, Language>,
}

fn tables() -> &'static Tables {
    static T: OnceLock<Tables> = OnceLock::new();
    T.get_or_init(|| {
        let mut by_lang = HashMap::new();
        let mut by_ext = HashMap::new();
        let mut by_name = HashMap::new();
        for d in DEFS.iter() {
            if let Some(l) = Language::from_name(d.name) {
                by_lang.insert(l, d);
                for e in d.extensions {
                    by_ext.insert(*e, l);
                }
                for f in d.filenames {
                    by_name.insert(*f, l);
                }
            }
        }
        Tables {
            by_lang,
            by_ext,
            by_name,
        }
    })
}

pub fn syntax_for(lang: Language) -> &'static Syntax {
    tables()
        .by_lang
        .get(&lang)
        .map(|d| &d.syntax)
        .unwrap_or(&UNKNOWN_SYNTAX)
}

pub fn from_extension(ext: &str) -> Option<Language> {
    tables().by_ext.get(ext.to_lowercase().as_str()).copied()
}

pub fn language_from_path(path: &Path) -> Option<Language> {
    let fname = path.file_name()?.to_string_lossy().to_lowercase();
    if let Some(l) = tables().by_name.get(fname.as_str()) {
        return Some(*l);
    }
    match path.extension() {
        Some(ext) => from_extension(&ext.to_string_lossy()),
        None => from_shebang(path),
    }
}

fn from_shebang(path: &Path) -> Option<Language> {
    use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader};
    let f = std::fs::File::open(path).ok()?;
    let mut reader = BufReader::new(f);
    let mut buf = Vec::new();
    reader.read_until(b'\n', &mut buf).ok()?;
    let line = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf).to_string();
    let mut words = line.split_whitespace();
    let first = words.next()?;
    if first == "#!/usr/bin/env" {
        let word = words.next()?;
        for d in DEFS.iter() {
            for e in d.env {
                if word.starts_with(e) {
                    return Language::from_name(d.name);
                }
            }
        }
        None
    } else {
        for d in DEFS.iter() {
            if d.shebangs.contains(&first) {
                return Language::from_name(d.name);
            }
        }
        None
    }
}

pub(crate) fn wrap(content: &str, hard_width: usize) -> String {
    let mut wrapper = wrap_algorithms::LineWrapper::new(hard_width);
    let mut total = Vec::new();
    for line in content.split_inclusive('\n') {
        wrapper.reset();

        total.extend(wrapper.wrap(line));
    }
    total.join("")
